<action type="say">
Here’s how I’d document and dispute those two charges.

Use wording like this for each transaction (you can paste into the “notes”/“explanation” field in the dispute form or read it to the agent):

1) Charge: 07/26 – $187.49 – “URBAN GEAR OUTLET MIAMI FL”  
Suggested explanation:
“I am disputing this $187.49 charge from ‘URBAN GEAR OUTLET MIAMI FL’ on 07/26. I did not make this purchase, I have never shopped at this merchant, and I did not authorize anyone else to use my card. My card was in my possession until I noticed it missing, and I reported it as stolen. Please treat this as an unauthorized charge related to my stolen card.”

2) Charge: 07/27 – $62.30 – “RAPIDRIDES TRANSPORT”  
Suggested explanation:
“I am disputing this $62.30 charge from ‘RAPIDRIDES TRANSPORT’ on 07/27. I did not make this transaction and did not authorize anyone else to use my card. I do not have an account with this merchant or service. My card was stolen and has already been reported as such. Please treat this as an unauthorized charge related to my stolen card.”

Next steps (app or by phone):

- In the app/website:  
  1) Open your credit card account.  
  2) Tap each of those two transactions.  
  3) Select “Report a problem” / “Dispute this charge” / similar.  
  4) Choose a reason like “Unauthorized – card lost or stolen.”  
  5) Paste the explanation text above (adjust if needed) and submit.

- By phone (if you prefer):  
  Call your card’s fraud line and say something like:
  “I’m calling to dispute two unauthorized charges on my credit card related to a card theft. The card has already been reported stolen and a replacement is on the way. The charges are:  
  • 07/26 – $187.49 – URBAN GEAR OUTLET MIAMI FL  
  • 07/27 – $62.30 – RAPIDRIDES TRANSPORT  
  I did not make or authorize these transactions and want to open fraud disputes for both.”

What to expect:
- The bank will usually:  
  - Open a fraud case for each transaction.  
  - Often issue a temporary credit while they investigate.  
  - Send you updates and possibly a form or email to confirm details.

If you tell me how you’re submitting (app vs phone) and your bank’s name (optional), I can tailor this into an even more direct, step‑by‑step script for their specific process.</action>
